headline: Philippine Coast Guard Receives Two Marine Protector-Class Patrol Vessels from US
seoTitle: PCG Receives Two US Marine Protector Patrol Vessels | FMB News
seoDescription: The Philippine Coast Guard has received two 27-meter Marine Protector-class patrol vessels from the United States to strengthen maritime safety and search and rescue.
keywords: Philippine Coast Guard Marine Protector vessels
deck: The two 27-meter vessels will enter Coast Guard service as BRP Pag-asa and BRP Patag after their expected arrival in Manila in October.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine Coast Guard has received two 27-meter Marine Protector-class patrol vessels from the United States, expanding its search-and-rescue, marine environmental protection and maritime-domain-awareness capabilities.
PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said the vessels will be commissioned as BRP Pag-asa (PATS-2701) and BRP Patag (PATS-2702) following their expected arrival in Manila in October 2026.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Twenty-four PCG crew members completed specialized operations and maintenance training for the vessels in Baltimore, Maryland, on August 20.

The transfer forms part of continuing Philippines-US maritime cooperation. The vessels are intended for maritime safety operations, emergency response and environmental incidents including oil spills.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Additional patrol vessels increase the Coast Guard's capacity to respond across the country's extensive maritime jurisdiction, where search-and-rescue, law enforcement and environmental missions often compete for limited assets.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next milestone is the vessels' expected Manila arrival in October and their formal commissioning into the Coast Guard fleet.
